title: Mandhana's Record-Breaking India Face Pakistan in Women's T20 Asia Cup Showdown
excerpt: India, riding Smriti Mandhana's historic 124 against Hong Kong, take on traditional rivals Pakistan in their final Group A match in Dubai on Saturday.
body:
• India face Pakistan in their final Women's T20 Asia Cup Group A match on Saturday at the Dubai International Stadium, with India already through to the semifinals.
  • Smriti Mandhana enters the fixture in record-breaking form after scoring 124 off 64 balls against Hong Kong to become the all-time highest run-scorer in women's international cricket.
  • Pakistan, captained by Fatima Sana, managed to defend only 119 against Thailand and remain overly reliant on opener Muneeba Ali and Sana with the all-round contributions.
  • India have won every Asia Cup meeting against Pakistan and are seven-time champions of the tournament.

India will look to cap a dominant group stage when they take on arch-rivals Pakistan in the final league match of the Women's T20 Asia Cup at the Dubai International Stadium on Saturday.

The seven-time champions have already booked their semifinal berth after wins over Thailand and Hong Kong, and will be eager to carry their momentum into the knockout phase. Pakistan, meanwhile, need a strong showing to keep their semifinal hopes alive after scraping past Thailand in their opener.

India's Ruthless Form

India have been the tournament's standout side. In their opener against Thailand on August 30, Deepti Sharma set a T20I record, and against Hong Kong on Thursday, Smriti Mandhana delivered a masterclass — 124 off 64 balls to become the all-time highest run-scorer in women's international cricket. India posted 193-5 and bowled Hong Kong out for 56, winning by 137 runs.

The opening pair of Mandhana and Shafali Verma has been devastating. Both batters have shown the ability to assess pitch conditions before accelerating, a crucial skill on the slower Dubai surfaces. Mandhana, named vice-captain for the tournament, is in the form of her life and could pass 11,000 career runs during the Asia Cup.

Head coach Amol Muzumdar has demanded aggressive cricket from his side, and the team has delivered. The pace attack has been bolstered by the emergence of Nandani Sharma alongside spearhead Kranti Gaud, while the spin department led by Deepti Sharma and Radha Yadav continues to strangle opposing batting lineups.

Pakistan's Batting Fragility

Pakistan enter the fixture under pressure. In their only match so far — against Thailand — they lost three wickets in the powerplay and limped to 119, a total they defended only because Thailand lacked the batting depth to chase it down.

The team remains heavily dependent on opener Muneeba Ali for runs at the top and captain Fatima Sana for all-round contributions. Unless Pakistan's middle order steps up, containing India's batting firepower will be only half the challenge.

"At the Asia level, no side comes close to India's level."

— NDTV Sports

The Rivalry's Broader Context

India-Pakistan fixtures in multi-team events have historically been one-sided affairs in women's cricket, with India dominating the head-to-head record. Pakistan's best results at the Women's Asia Cup came in 2012 and 2016, when they finished runners-up — losing to India in both finals.

India, however, have their own motivation beyond the rivalry. They were stunned by Sri Lanka in the 2024 final and are determined to reclaim the title. Coach Muzumdar has identified the need for a deeper pool of power-hitters and fast bowlers if India are to challenge Australia's global dominance, and this tournament serves as a proving ground ahead of the Asian Games.

What's Next

The match starts at 8 PM IST on Saturday. A win would give India a perfect group-stage record heading into the semifinals, scheduled for September 10 and 11, with the final on September 13. For Pakistan, anything less than a competitive display would raise serious questions about the direction of their women's program.
